title: All Orderings

story.briefing: The lock will accept exactly one arrangement of the key fragments, and nobody remembers which. Enumerate every arrangement so the Core can try them in order.
story.success: Every arrangement enumerated. The lock yields on the seventh try.

description: Given an array of distinct integers, return every possible ordering of them. The orderings must appear in increasing lexicographic order — compare two orderings by their first differing position. An empty input returns a list containing one empty ordering.

examples.explanation: Sorted order first, regardless of the input order.
One ordering exists: the empty one.

hints: Build one ordering position by position. At each position try every value not yet used, then undo that choice and try the next.
The required output order falls out for free if you sort the values first and always try them smallest to largest. Do not sort the results afterwards.
Sort the input. Recurse carrying a partial ordering and a used-marker per value. When the partial ordering is full, record a copy of it — a copy, not the array itself, which you are about to modify.
